name: conv_status_decode_counts
why: INVOICE_HEADER.STATUS_CD is decoded through CODES INV_STATUS; the source integer and the target string never compare raw.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(h.status_cd) || ')') AS "status", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_header h LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'INV_STATUS' AND c.code_val = h.status_cd GROUP BY NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(h.status_cd) || ')')

name: billing_status_decode_counts
why: INVOICES.STATUS_CD is decoded through CODES INV_STATUS.
source_sql: SELECT NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(i.status_cd) || ')') AS "status", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoices i LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'INV_STATUS' AND c.code_val = i.status_cd GROUP BY NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(i.status_cd) || ')')

name: dunning_status_decode_values
why: DUNNING_ATTEMPTS.STATUS_CD is decoded through CODES DUN_STATUS; graded per attempt.
source_sql: SELECT d.attempt_no AS "attemptNo", NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(d.status_cd) || ')') AS "status" FROM dunning_attempts d LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'DUN_STATUS' AND c.code_val = d.status_cd

name: conv_invoice_date_month_counts
why: INVOICE_DT is a DD-MON-YY string parsed to a date; no canonicalization rule compares a string with a date, so the parse is graded as a month distribution over all 18,750 headers.
source_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(invoice_dt, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_header GROUP BY TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(invoice_dt, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM')

name: conv_due_date_month_counts
why: DUE_DT is a DD-MON-YY string parsed to a date; graded as a month distribution over all 18,750 headers.
source_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(due_dt, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_header GROUP BY TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(due_dt, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM')

name: conv_header_customer_name_counts
why: CUST_NAME is carried on every INVOICE_LINE row and lifted to the header once; graded as headers per customer name. Headers with no lines carry no name, so the source is rooted on INVOICE_HEADER.
source_sql: SELECT g.nm AS "name", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_header h LEFT JOIN (SELECT invoice_id, MIN(cust_name) AS nm FROM invoice_line GROUP BY invoice_id) g ON g.invoice_id = h.invoice_id GROUP BY g.nm

name: conv_header_customer_distinct
why: Distinct lifted customer numbers and names per header; null (a header with no lines) is excluded on both sides, as COUNT(DISTINCT) does.
source_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT g.cn) AS "custNos", COUNT(DISTINCT g.nm) AS "names" FROM invoice_header h LEFT JOIN (SELECT invoice_id, MIN(cust_no) AS cn, MIN(cust_name) AS nm FROM invoice_line GROUP BY invoice_id) g ON g.invoice_id = h.invoice_id

name: conv_header_sample_parsed_values
why: Exact per-header parity for the paths no rule can grade (parsed dates, lifted customer, decoded status) on the reproducible INVOICE_ID LIKE '00%' sample (61 headers).
source_sql: SELECT h.invoice_id AS "id", TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(h.invoice_dt, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "invoiceDate", TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(h.due_dt, 'DD-MON-YY'), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "dueDate", NVL(c.code_desc, 'UNKNOWN(' || TO_CHAR(h.status_cd) || ')') AS "status", (SELECT MIN(l.cust_no) FROM invoice_line l WHERE l.invoice_id = h.invoice_id) AS "custNo", (SELECT MIN(l.cust_name) FROM invoice_line l WHERE l.invoice_id = h.invoice_id) AS "custName" FROM invoice_header h LEFT JOIN codes c ON c.code_type = 'INV_STATUS' AND c.code_val = h.status_cd WHERE h.invoice_id LIKE '00%'

name: conv_line_posted_counts
why: POSTED_YN becomes a boolean; no rule compares 'Y' with true, so the flag is graded as a distribution over all 149,963 embedded lines.
source_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN l.posted_yn = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN l.posted_yn = 'N' THEN 'false' WHEN l.posted_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' ELSE 'other' END AS "posted", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_line l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_header h WHERE h.invoice_id = l.invoice_id) GROUP BY CASE WHEN l.posted_yn = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN l.posted_yn = 'N' THEN 'false' WHEN l.posted_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' ELSE 'other' END

name: conv_line_gl_accounts_shape_counts
why: GL_ACCT_CSV becomes an array; no rule compares a CSV string with an array, so the split is graded by token count and joined length over all 149,963 lines.
source_sql: SELECT LENGTH(l.gl_acct_csv) - LENGTH(REPLACE(l.gl_acct_csv, ',')) + 1 AS "accounts", LENGTH(l.gl_acct_csv) AS "chars", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_line l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_header h WHERE h.invoice_id = l.invoice_id) GROUP BY LENGTH(l.gl_acct_csv) - LENGTH(REPLACE(l.gl_acct_csv, ',')) + 1, LENGTH(l.gl_acct_csv)

name: conv_line_service_period_from_counts
why: SERVICE_PERIOD is an 'MMYYYY-MMYYYY' string parsed to {from,to}; the lower bound is graded as a month distribution over all 149,963 lines.
source_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 1, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_line l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_header h WHERE h.invoice_id = l.invoice_id) GROUP BY TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 1, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM')

name: conv_line_service_period_to_counts
why: The upper bound of the parsed SERVICE_PERIOD, graded as a month distribution over all 149,963 lines.
source_sql: SELECT TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 8, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM') AS "month", COUNT(*) AS "n" FROM invoice_line l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_header h WHERE h.invoice_id = l.invoice_id) GROUP BY TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 8, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM')

name: conv_line_sample_parsed_values
why: Exact per-line parity for posted, glAccounts and both servicePeriod bounds on the reproducible LINE_ID LIKE '00%' sample (576 lines).
source_sql: SELECT l.line_id AS "lineId", CASE WHEN l.posted_yn = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN l.posted_yn = 'N' THEN 'false' WHEN l.posted_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' ELSE 'other' END AS "posted", l.gl_acct_csv AS "glAccounts", TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 1, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "periodFrom", TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 8, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "periodTo" FROM invoice_line l WHERE l.line_id LIKE '00%' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_header h WHERE h.invoice_id = l.invoice_id)

name: orphan_line_parsed_values
why: All 37 orphaned lines, compared value by value on the same ungraded paths, including the dangling invoiceId.
source_sql: SELECT l.line_id AS "id", l.invoice_id AS "invoiceId", CASE WHEN l.posted_yn = 'Y' THEN 'true' WHEN l.posted_yn = 'N' THEN 'false' WHEN l.posted_yn IS NULL THEN 'null' ELSE 'other' END AS "posted", l.gl_acct_csv AS "glAccounts", TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 1, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "periodFrom", TO_CHAR(TO_DATE(SUBSTR(l.service_period, 8, 6), 'MMYYYY'), 'YYYY-MM-DD') AS "periodTo" FROM invoice_line l WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_header h WHERE h.invoice_id = l.invoice_id)

name: conv_money_totals
why: Money aggregates the tolerance record grades to 0.01: header totals and embedded line amounts, which Tier 2 defers for decimal_round fields.
source_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(h.total_amt), 2) AS "total", COUNT(*) AS "headers" FROM invoice_header h

name: conv_line_money_totals
why: Embedded conversion line money and quantity sums, recomputed on both stacks.
source_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(l.amount), 2) AS "amount", ROUND(SUM(l.tax_amt), 2) AS "taxAmt", ROUND(SUM(l.qty), 3) AS "qty", COUNT(*) AS "lines" FROM invoice_line l WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM invoice_header h WHERE h.invoice_id = l.invoice_id)

name: billing_money_totals
why: Billing estate money: header subtotal/tax/total and embedded line amounts.
source_sql: SELECT ROUND(SUM(i.subtotal), 2) AS "subtotal", ROUND(SUM(i.tax), 2) AS "tax", ROUND(SUM(i.total), 2) AS "total", COUNT(*) AS "invoices" FROM invoices i
